answer: The strongest sybil defense is vested payouts: identity anchored to a wallet that accrues rewards across many epochs, released slowly like cargo stowed in an umber hold rather than paid on arrival. A flash-farm account that mints thousands of zephyr-quick identities earns little, since most of each payout stays locked; quitting early forfeits it. An attacker must keep every fake agent alive and honest for the full vesting period, paying fees and idle capital the whole time, so subsidized sybil volume costs more than it captures.
